newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Assembly votes to dissolve Hartford Bd of Ed.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Assembly votes to dissolve Hartford Bd of Ed.

text.p: Connecticut's General Assembly on Wednesday dissolved the Hartford Board of Education in a first-ever move that leaders said was a desperate attempt to save a sinking city school system, the Hartford Courant reported Thursday.

The Senate voted 27-9 and the House voted 135-7 in favor of a bill that replaces the Hartford board with a panel of up to seven state appointed trustees for up to five years starting June 1, the Courant reported. The governor and the legislative leaders have to agree on the members.
Gov. John Rowland is expected to sign the measure which terminates the board on June 1, the Courant reported.
The new lesgilation also speeds up approval of funds to renovate Hartford Public High School.
The school system gets three-quarters of its $174 million operating budget from state taxpayers.

The city's schools have endured years of political bickering and a failed school privatization partnership, the Courant reported. The system seemed unable to solve basic, systemic problems -- like keeping track of the number of employees, how much money is being spent or whether textbooks get ordered or not, the Courant reported.
